captions.instagram:
Three write-offs we see hair stylists skip, especially booth renters and 1099 stylists:

✔️ Card processing fees. Square or Stripe keeps its cut before the money reaches your bank. Report the full sales, then deduct the fees.
✔️ Classes that sharpen skills you already use, like an advanced color course. (Beauty school to get licensed doesn't count.)
✔️ Shears, dryers and flat irons. The work share counts, and many tools can be written off the year you buy them.

Our Hair Stylist & Salon Bookkeeping Tracker keeps booth rent, tips, fees and supplies in one place all year.

sources.fact: Processor fees (Square, Stripe) are deductible; report full sales and deduct the fees (repo data/deductions.json bank-card-fees, checked 2026-10-21)

Education that maintains or improves skills in your current business is deductible; education for a new trade or minimum entry requirements is not (data/deductions.json business-education, checked 2026-10-21)
Tools: business share deductible; many can be expensed under the de minimis safe harbor or Section 179 (data/deductions.json tools-equipment, checked 2026-10-21)
De minimis safe harbor: $2,500 per item/invoice, annual election
